item.title: Chelsea frustrated by Hacken in women's Champions League, Man City win
item.description: Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk frustrated Chelsea (Adam Ihse/TT) Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition. The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay. Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand. However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal -- both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor's side -- could leapfrog them this matchday. "It's a frustrating result," Blues boss Bompastor told UEFA. "We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn't go that way. We need to learn from this." Women's Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings. A first-half Aoba Fujino brace cancelled out Elisa Bartoli's opener for the hosts by half-time. Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table. Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference. Klara Buehl's strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek's early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position. Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on. PSG lie in ninth place on five points. In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes. A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada's side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points. Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after. Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder's reverse pass. "It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn't won any of our first three games," Caruso said. "We have to try to finish among the top teams." Roma held on to beat Swiss side Servette 2-1. On Wednesday, eight-time winners Lyon are in action away to Juventus. nf/lp

item.title: Zé Lucas rallies fans for Belém U20 games: “Our home, this is Brazil”
item.description: Zé Lucas rallies fans for Belém U20 games: “Our home, this is Brazil” Brazil’s Under-20 national team continued preparations on Tuesday (10) for their friendlies against Peru at the Mangueirão in Belém. Tuesday (10) marked the first training session in which coach Paulo Victor had the full squad at his disposal. One of the team’s key players, defensive midfielder Zé Lucas spoke about adapting to the climate and the stadium, and revealed that, as the first match approaches, the players are starting to feel the benefits of home advantage: “This is our home, this is Brazil.” A good performance starts with settling in well. Defensive midfielder Zé Lucas said Brazil’s Under-20 team are excited about Belém, “a new city unlocked” for most of the players. “We’re adapting to the city too, a new city for us as Brazil players. It’s a new city unlocked,” he said. Zé Lucas during a ball drill at the Mangueirão as Brazil’s Under-20 team prepare for their friendlies against Peru Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF Known for its passion for football, the capital of Pará has the players excited about the prospect of fan support. The midfielder spoke about the squad’s anticipation of playing in front of the crowd, called on fans to come out and promised a committed performance to put on a good show. “Our expectations couldn’t be higher, because this is our home, this is Brazil. So I believe the fans will turn out in numbers and support us, as they’ve always supported Brazil. Regardless of the age group, if it’s the Brazilian national team, the fans are there. So we’re really looking forward to that, and we hope we can repay all their support on the pitch with plenty of effort, fight and determination, wearing a shirt that carries so much history,” he said. A South American Under-17 champion in 2025, Zé Lucas aims to repeat the achievement with the Under-20 team in 2027 Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF Zé Lucas speaks from experience when he mentions the unwavering support across all age groups. In 2025, he won the South American title with Brazil’s Under-17 team under coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci. Now working with Paulo Victor in Brazil’s yellow shirt, he hopes to repeat that success by winning the Under-20 competition. “Last year, Patetuci gave me a lot of confidence. Coach Paulo Victor is also giving us a lot of confidence here, not just me, but the whole squad. The group feels relaxed and ready to do what he asks and deliver in the best way possible,” he said. Tuesday’s session focused on refining the team’s playing style, with drills involving movement, passing, crossing and finishing. Training also included work on attacking and defensive organisation. Brazil face Peru on the 13th and 16th. Both matches kick off at 8 p.m. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that! The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind. Although, admittedly, Cronin’s biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market. The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later. Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can’t. Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him. But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn’t quite pass the smell test. Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary. So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction. And if you’re being honest, you probably don’t need to wonder which of the two it is. “We were very focused and we’ll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can,” Cronin said. That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks. But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard’s career? “Dame literally just wants to win,” said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. “I think that’s the only thing left he really has to (do). He’s already proven he’s a winner, but at the highest level.” Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon? Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he’s just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn’t cost the Blazers much to try. However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard’s swan song. If you don’t get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer . And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season. The franchise icon certainly hasn’t said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant’s presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through. When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, “My position on it was, I’m prepared for whatever.” It’s good that he’s already thinking about other positions. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. The Tigers this offseason decided to part ways with veteran closer Kenley Jansen, two saves shy of him reaching 500 for his career. Finnegan will be back for 2027, and it's likely he'll have some a new bullpen mate or three as Harris acknowledged the minor-league pipeline to the back end of the bullpen isn't where the organization wants it. "So we're going to have to find different acquisition avenues to add to our 'pen right now," Harris said. If the Tigers do go shopping for a closer-type reliever, veteran right-handed closers David Bednar, 32, and Raisel Iglesias, 36, are two of the top names on the market. If the Tigers want to try rehabbing a player who had a down 2026, right-hander Bryan Abreu, 29, could be a way to go on a shorter-term deal. Hinch is familiar with Abreu from their time together with the Houston Astros. The Tigers had few success stories to speak of with emerging relievers in 2026, outside of perhaps lefty Drew Sommers and right-hander Jacob Waguespack, who was acquired in a June trade with the Milwaukee Brewers, posted a 1.3 WAR and recently resigned for 2027 on a one-year, $1.3-million contract . Right-hander Burch Smith had his moments, too. But of the Tigers' top 30 prospects, as ranked by MLB Pipeline, there are no major league-ready relievers outside of lefty Andrew Sears (No. 13), who had a 7.11 in a small sample (six games) with the Tigers down the stretch. "Longer term, we want to be able to produce homegrown bullpens that can pitch together, stay together, and get better together," Harris said. "I think we're well on our way to doing it, but this offseason we've got to find a way to add to our 'pen externally because the homegrown arms we've been trading for, drafting, developing, haven't all gotten there." Drew Anderson also was signed last winter and returns to the Tigers in 2027 after they picked up his $10-million option . But Anderson seemed to find his comfort zone as a starter more than a reliever in 2026. Their starters include Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Anderson, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan (acquired in the Skubal trade), as well as Reese Olson, who is expected back after missing the entire 2026 season with shoulder surgery. Any rotation additions wouldn't seem likely to be on long-term deals. (In other words, don't hold your breath on a Tarik Skubal reunion.) "We like the group of young starters that are coming up through the minor leagues," Harris said. "We also like the young starters that are in the big leagues. "We've gotta make sure we build the right bridge between those two groups." MLB free-agency is likely to pick the pace in the coming days , ahead of a likely lockout when the Collective Bargaining Agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. Dec. 1. item.title: The southpaw flamethrower
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 03: Adrian Morejon #50 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers during the seventh inning in game one of the National League Division Series at American Family Field on October 03, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Adrian Morejon When the Padres signed Adrian Morejon out of Cuba in 2016, it was a big deal. At the time, the left-hander was ranked second overall among international prospects. The 17-year-old came over and began to pitch quite well as a starting pitcher, posting a sub-4.00 ERA in his first two minor-league seasons. Morejon made his debut in 2019 and struggled to find his footing. His stuff never quite played out as a starter, so San Diego transitioned him into the bullpen. Injuries held him back, with Morejon throwing just 47 2/3 big-league innings from 2021-23. Overall Grade: A- Then, everything changed. In 2024, Morejon became one of the most dominant relief pitchers in baseball. He took it to another level in 2025 and was nearly as good in ‘26. Morejon twirled a career-high 86 innings, posting a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP and .205 opponent batting average. He accumulated 107 strikeouts and 1.9 bWAR in that time. His only problem were blips in April (6.43 ERA) and September (4.50 ERA). His underlying metrics are even better. Morejon’s expected stats (xERA and xBA) are both roughly 50 points lower than his actual marks. His sinker was one of the best in baseball (+11 Pitching Run Value), ranking him fifth among all relievers in PRV. item.content:encoded: Catcher Ivan Luciano might just be the only option at DH, literally Introduction If you haven’t read any of the previous articles in my D-backs Prospect All-Star series, I’ve been breaking down the best 2026 seasons at each position in the D-backs Farm system since the MiLB regular season ended. Just to recap, in part one, we looked at our starting pitcher, catcher, and the infield corner positions. TLDR: That gave us Carlos Virahonda as the starting catcher, David Hagaman as starting pitcher; At the hot corner, we have Danny Serretti as our third baseman, and across the diamond we have at first base, Manuel Pena . In part two, we looked at the middle infield along with the outfield . TLDR: Our all star infield is anchored by the D-backs’ top two overall prospects, second baseman Demetrio Crisantes and shortstop Kayson Cunningham . The outfield was much more an unknown factor, but we’ll say it’s Jeremy Surriel , Trent Youngblood , and Yohendi Hernandez Last week, we looked at my reliever of the year Joe Ariola. That just leaves us with one position unaccounted for, and if you hadn’t figured it out from the title, it’s designated hitter. It is truly sad that we have to have this conversation but.. DH Prospects aren’t really a thing I should really address the massive elephant in the room: a “Designated Hitter prospect” is a borderline oxymoronic term. If you’re an actual ranked prospect and you are a primary DH, this can only be for a few reasons, some of which are borderline or outright hypothetical. You are so bad defensively that everyone else decided that you don’t need that baseball glove anymore, but your bat is that good. There are better players at your competent positions, and nowhere else to play you where you aren’t a liability, but your bat is legitimately good enough that the team will fit your bat into the lineup. You are an injury risk and/or coming off a serious injury. You are a successful amateur two-way player, but the team doesn’t think you’re good enough at pitching to continue doing both. All of the above You are the proverbial unicorn, an actual two way player, who would completely dominate the league’s batters/pitchers if you’d just wasting your talent trying to do both.***** “No the team isn’t going to have you playing the field, in-between your starts, making diving catches in left. I don’t care that you’d be a better right fielder “^ ***** No one in Arizona or any other MLB team’s farm systems is this, or even looks like they might be this right now, thanks to the current two-way player rule ^Ohtani actually suggested this to all the professional teams he has played for (citation Needed) . Signing an amateur prospect who’s exclusively a DH is basically unheard of, at least in my experience. Even when converting a two-way DH/Pitcher to DH, that player is going to be given every chance to learn how to play the field. The Diamondbacks have generally used the DH position in the minors as a way to give the regulars a rest, and have mostly avoided having DH-exclusive hitters. Finding our D-backs MiLB All-Star DH There are a few ways we can go about finding a DH for our MILB All-Star team. We could just go with highest wRC+/OPS in the D-backs farm. That would be Weber Neels , a 19th round pick in this year draft who hit .365/.411/.750 with a 179 wRC+. That guy smashed eleven doubles and three homeruns in the span of twelve games in his professional debut with Low A Visalia. Pack it up and go because we find our guy. What’s that? He only played 12 games total and played the field in every game so you think he doesn’t count? Well then, I’m sure if I go with Tim Tawa and his .320/.409/.733 triple slash with a 161 wRC+ for Triple A Reno, you’re going to complain that twenty games isn’t much better and then I’ll point out he wouldn’t count anyway since he’s not a prospect anymore and I excluded any player with MLB service time in this discussion. Okay, fine, we’ll go back to taking this seriously. The Diamondbacks have just three qualified hitters at DH in their entire MILB farm system. Two of those hitters, 17 year old catcher/DH Jhosep Villarroel and 1B/OF/DH Manny Almonte played in the Dominican Summer League, which has a very short season and a bunch of other issues that compound the difficulty of evaluating prospects. That leaves with only one qualified hitter in the in upper levels of the minor leagues in the Dbacks organization that had enough plate appearences to qualify at DH, and that’s Catcher Ivan Luciano. Jhosep Villarroel had a extremely impressive debut season, putting up triple slash of .303/.500/.485 with a 148 wRC+, it was in only 47 games AND in the DSL. Manny Almonte’s batting line of .255/.372/.465 with a 92 wRC+ was squarely below average, so he’s out as an option at DH, on top of the same reasons as Villarroel. That leaves us with just the one option to plug in at DH, the aforementioned Ivan Luciano. Luciano is a legit catching prospect, but he had to share time with a plethora of other (arguably better) catching prospects like Carlos Virahonda. If there weren’t better options on Visalia or Hillsboro’s rosters, I dont think he’d have spent as much time DHing as he did in 2026. In 85 games with the Low A level Visalia Rawhide, the 19 year old Luciano hit .264/.375/.441 with a 109 wRC+. Luciano spent the remaining 12 games of his 2026 season playing for the High-A level Hillsboro Hops, where he hit .279/.380/.465 with a 122 wRC+. In 97 games combined across the two levels in 2026, Luciano hit .266/.376/.444 with a 111 wRC+. Luciano isn’t a bad pick to DH, just like he wasn’t a bad pick for an honorable mention/runner up for all-star to Virahonda at catcher. Villarroel’s season was as worthy of a mention here just like it was when going over the catching position, but Luciano gets the nod, from playing twice as many games at a higher level on the minor league ladder. Not Every Team Treats MILB DHs like the D-backs While finishing up the research for this article, I found a rather surprising piece of information: There’s actually 96 total qualified DHs in MiLB . Out of the thirty MLB franchises there were two teams who didn’t have a qualified hitter at DH, along with four teams that have just one. Seventeen other teams match the D-backs with at least three hitters qualified at DH. The Cincinnati Reds lead the way with seven. Out of the 96 qualified designated hitters in Minor League Baseball, 67 of them have a 100 wRC+ or better. Jhosep Villarroel’s 148 wRC+ looks even better when compared to his peers; his 2026 season was the fourth best out of all the qualified DHs, and the three hitters who had better seasons were old for the levels they were assigned. Meanwhile, Luciano’s 111 wRC+ is tied for 43rd, which doesn’t sound particularly impressive, but like Villarroel, there are quite a few hitters ahead of him who were old for their assigned level, or are just outright not a prospect. So what does this all mean? I don’t think the presence or lack of DH “prospects’ really means anything other than what I wrote in the first half the article. They are clearly an afterthought in minor league player development. There is basically no correlation with being members of the the formerly DH-less National League. I guess the real question here is should the D-backs put more into developing some full-time hitters at the DH position, or should they continue the approach of having no approach? Who would you put as THE DH on the 2026 D-backs Prospect All-Star team? Let me me know in the comments!

item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive end Austin Booker (94) reacts after a play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. Be honest: how many of you guys had the Chicago Bears at 7-2 and in first place at the bye? There’s a long way to go, but at the midpoint of the 2026 season, the Bears look like a legit threat to win the NFC. I know it’s cliché to say, but the bye is really hitting at an opportune time for the Bears. The running back room should get a boost with D’Andre Swift able to rest up and Kyle Monangai seemingly ready to return from his toe/thumb injury. Wideout Luther Burden III, who has 49 receptions and 644 receiving yards, exited the win over the Bucs with a concussion, so he needs the break. With how much the offense has dominated the time of possession through the first nine games, the offensive line could use some relaxing time away. The Bears didn’t add anything else to the defense at the trade deadline, but the huge trade for Jeffery Simmons paid immediate dividends. He’s a force multiplier who makes everyone better. Rookie Malik Muhammad II, who has been the Bears’ best corner, should be back after the bye. Jaylon Johnson has had a rough start to the season but is coming off his best game. Kyler Gordon and Tyrique Stevenson were both dinged up on Sunday night, so a week away will do them good, and defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo should be back from injured reserve soon. I also think the extra week for Caleb Williams to stew over his four-pick game will lead to an even hungrier player in the second half. The Bears are in a great place to continue their quest for back-to-back playoff appearances. How many wins will the Bears have? Are you confident in the Bears? item.title: Celtics lottery pick Aaron Nesmith on the importance of opportunity
item.description: MEXICO CITY - To Aaron Nesmith, opportunity matters. The former Vanderbilt alum has found exactly that with the team the Boston Celtics traded him to, Nesmith having carved out a role on the wing with the Indiana Pacers , his trademark style of physical play and shooting a key part of Indiana's approach to the game. The Celtics Wire caught up with him in Mexico City for the 2026 NBA Mexico City Game, where his Pacers squad fell to Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets . "We're a team that's very dependent on one another for our success, and we've got to have everybody firing in all at all on all cylinders at all times," said Indiana head coach Rick Carlisle of his import to the team after the loss. And while the Pacers may not have come back home with a win for their efforts, Nesmith still saw value in simply making the trip to Mexico. "Even being from the U.S., I didn't get the chance to see NBA players as a kid," said Nesmith. "So for these kids to be able to see us play, it's an honor coming out to their home country." Opportunity (or it's lack) also helped hasten the end of his time with the Celtics, the South Carolina native finding doors open to him in Indiana that were never going to with a stacked roster ahead of him in Boston. "You've got to be able to make mistakes and learn from those mistakes," said Nesmith. "People don't get better by looking over their shoulder. They get better by giving 100 percent." With the Pacers, the opportunity is there, and so far, so has the effort. And with injuries derailing the start of what was supposed to a bounce-back campaign for Indiana, the former Celtic's team will need him to be better than ever. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Images Jacksonville Jaguars: Added Jessie Bates III, Davon Godchaux, Jordan Davis The Jags’ additions make little impact on the cap this season, and both Bates and Godchaux are expiring deals. The Jaguars would potentially want to retain both Bates and Godchaux (the latter at a relatively low figure), especially since Trevor Lawrence remains on a manageable deal (five years, $278 million) through 2031. San Francisco 49ers: Added DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen Not only do the 49ers have the NFL’s top record, but they also have a ton of cap space ($31 million, which ranks fifth in the league, according to Spotrac ). And better still for San Francisco, both are expiring deals and don’t necessarily need to be brought back if they opt not to. There’s the potential issue of $80 million owed to Cousins across 2027 and 2028 if Minnesota opts to keep him (would add some cap constraints that don’t currently apply). But that would likely be declined instead, forcing the Vikings to either try and bring him back on a cheaper deal or make some bigger moves to bring in a long-term QB solution finally. Seattle Seahawks: Added Quenton Nelson Seattle has cap space this year and next, and brought in Nelson on an expiring deal. If the team chooses to bring him back next year, they can fit him in under the current cap number. But if they don’t, it leaves upwards of $30 million to play with to handle the rest of its business right now. Indianapolis Colts: Traded away Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson The Colts didn’t trade bigger names like Jonathan Taylor or Daniel Jones, but did move four players in exchange for a net of five picks over the course of the 2027 and 2028 drafts. None of those are firsts, which makes it harder to acquire the elite talent needed to reset the roster. But also easier to address numerous areas of need with smaller salaries. Indianapolis will have a staggering $77 million in cap space next year, so could also use that room to make significant upgrades via free agency. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: What Mets’ David Stearns said about Bo Bichette’s contract decision

As the New York Mets are surrounded by rumors heading into the offseason, one thing is certain: Bo Bichette will return to the team, opting into his player option. With Bichette returning to the Mets , it has garnered an enthusiastic reaction from President of Baseball Operations David Stearns. Speaking at MLB’s annual general managers’ meetings, Stearns was asked about Bichette coming back to the team for the 2027 season, as the 28-year-old recorded a .260 batting average with 18 home runs and 78 RBIs. Stearns didn’t hesitate to express his excitement about Bichette returning, saying that New York expects him to “have a really good year next year” and that he has been “emerging as a leader” with the ball club. “I was happy about it. We expect Bo to have a really good year next year; we saw what he’s capable of doing over the last three, four months of the season, and I think he is excited to come back,” Stearns said, according to SNY Mets. “He’s comfortable with our group, he’s emerging as a leader in our clubhouse, and I’m very excited to have him back.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) David Stearns says he's "very excited" to have Bo Bichette back with the Mets next season: "We expect Bo to have a really good year next year. We saw what he's capable of doing over the last 3-4 months of the season." pic.twitter.com/RMVSBaIyP1 — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) November 10, 2026 Bichette signed with the Mets last offseason on a three-year, $126 million that came with a player option, leading to him making the decision to come back to the team. Though it was a slow start for the former Toronto Blue Jay, he finished strong, hitting a .285 batting average in the second half of the season. At any rate, Bichette looks to improve along with New York after finushing with a 74-88 record, putting them last in the NL East. item.title: Yankees’ bench coach officially linked to Astros’ manager job
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Yankees’ bench coach officially linked to Astros’ manager job appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Astros are still looking for their next manager. The Astros already addressed their general manager opening by hiring Randy Flores . As for their manager opening, Houston was recently linked to New York Yankees ’ bench coach Brad Ausmus. On Tuesday, Yankees general manager Brian Cashman officially confirmed that Ausmus is a candidate for the Astros’ manager job, via Jorge Castillo of ESPN. “Brian Cashman confirmed Brad Ausmus is a candidate for the Astros’ managerial job (and was a candidate for their GM job),” Castillo reported. Ausmus played at the big league level from 1993-2010. He earned one All-Star selection and three Gold Glove Awards during his MLB career. Ausmus spent 10 of his 18 years with the Astros, so coaching in Houston would serve as a reunion. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He has big league managing experience as well. He led the Detroit Tigers from 2014-2017. Detroit had two winning seasons under Ausmus, including a 90-win 2014 campaign. Ausmus would go on to manage the Los Angeles Angels in 2019 as well. He has been the Yankees’ bench coach since 2024. The Astros have also been connected to Albert Pujols . While the slugger who hit 703 home runs (fourth all-time) hasn’t managed in MLB, he does have managing experience in the World Baseball Classic. He’d have no trouble earning respect given his Hall of Fame resume as a player. There will be other candidates as well, but Ausmus and Pujols are certainly in the conversation. The only other manager opening at the moment is the Angels’ job. It remains to be seen if Ausmus would have any interest in returning to Anaheim. If the Astros go in a different direction, it wouldn’t be surprising to see Ausmus maintain his role with the Yankees in 2027. item.title: NFL Makes Announcement Involving Kenneth Walker III
item.description: The NFL made an announcement on Monday involving Kansas City Chiefs star Kenneth Walker III. It came a day after his strong Week 9 performance in his team’s 35-12 win over the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium. The running back recorded 18 rushing attempts for 102 yards and one touchdown. He added four receptions for two yards and two more scores. Walker has been on fire this year and picked up where he left off after winning the Super Bowl and Super Bowl MVP honors with the Seattle Seahawks last season. More importantly, the Chiefs snapped their two-game skid and returned to their winning ways. Patrick Mahomes led the offense with 23-of-31 completions for 242 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. Meanwhile, Travis Kelce powered the receiving corps with four receptions for 72 yards, while Rashee Rice added five catches for 49 yards. NFL: Seattle Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III speaks during the Super Bowl LX winning head coach and most valuable player press conference. NFL Nominates Kenneth Walker III for Weekly Award The NFL released the second group of nominees for the Air & Ground Players of the Week. One of them is Walker, and the league included his stats versus the Jets. Joining him on the list are the Dallas Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb and the Los Angeles Rams’ Puka Nacua. It also asked fans to vote on who they believe deserves to win the honor. “The second group of nominees for the @FedEx Air & Ground Players of the Week. Vote for your winner below!” the NFL wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) Walker joined Kansas City in the offseason as a free agent. He signed a three-year, $45 million contract in March, giving the team a lot of experience and another weapon Mahomes can maximize. The 26-year-old has not disappointed with his big performances and will be key down the stretch as the Chiefs look to reclaim lost glory. They have their sights set on returning to playoffs after missing it last season for the first time in Mahomes QB1 era. item.title: Kyle Busch posthumously wins NASCAR Cup Most Popular Driver Award
item.description: Motorsport photo Kyle Busch is the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Most Popular Driver, becoming just the second driver to ever win the award posthumously, joining fellow Richard Childress Racing driver and seven-time Cup champion Dale Earnhardt, who won the award after his death in a crash at the end of the 2001 Daytona 500. Busch's wife Samantha attended the banquet and accepted the award on his behalf. Following the tragic passing of the two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion, there was an immediate push for him to be named Most Popular Driver for the 2026 season. When the voting officially began, Chase Elliott , who has won the award every year since 2018, withdrew his name from consideration and urged his fans to vote for Busch. Some wondered if Carson Hocevar would win the award due to his explosive fandom growth in the last few months, and while he did not withdraw his own name, he urged his fans to vote for Busch as well. It's a special gesture for a polarizing driver who was often booed throughout his career, though his popularity among the fans improved quite a bit in recent years. “I know he’s up there like, ’There you go, I did that.’” Samantha on Kyle Busch winning NASCAR’s Most Popular Driver by a landslide. ❤️ https://t.co/A5TdYHxCL6 — Motorsport (@Motorsport) November 11, 2026 Busch is also the first driver not named Earnhardt or Elliott to win the award since Darrell Waltrip in 1990. Busch won a record 234 races across all three national divisions, with the final win coming in a Truck race just days before his passing at the age of 41. He died as the result of pneumonia that progressed into sepsis, and since then, there's been a flood of tributes and honors for the NASCAR legend every race weekend. Bill Elliott holds the record for Most Popular Driver awards in the Cup Series at 16, followed by Dale Earnhardt Jr. with 15, Richard Petty with nine, Chase Elliott with eight, and Bobby Allison with seven. In the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, newly crowned two-time series champion Justin Allgaier won the Most Popular Driver award for the fourth consecutive year and the seventh time in his career. In the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series, championship runner-up Layne Riggs earned his first Most Popular Driver award. It’s lighthearted reading designed to entertain, maybe even inform, and perhaps spark a few memories and a touch of debate. Or, if you prefer, a rage-bait waste of time that shames the internet. Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé. Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. And true, it might be a challenging read for those (and, let’s be clear, we’re absolutely definitely not referring to ourselves here, no sirree) old enough to have been brought up in an era of 1; 2, 5, 6, 3; 7, 4, 8, 11; 9 (big man), 10 (little man). The days of two substitutes who wore Nos 12 and 14. The days of a quarter of wine gums in your pocket and misty rain drifting across the floodlights and … oh my god Asamoah Gyan is wearing No 3 and playing up front. This is not a drill. Repeat this is not a drill. Burn it all down, the game’s gone. There is something about it all that does invoke strangely strong reactions, but every day is a school day. item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.description: United and City dominate the news cycle with stories so strange and vast they threaten to consume the rest of the league In Manchester this weekend it was possible to bookend your Thursday‑to‑Sunday entertainment with two cultural events. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
